From: Aditi Sharma <aditi.sharma@northwindrobotics.com>
To: ap@ferrocraft-industries.com

I sent Ferrocraft's AP inbox invoice NWR-2287 on Monday and it bounced silently in Gmail's queue for three days before this notice finally surfaced — worth knowing, because I'd assumed it went through and Ilya had already logged it as sent in the AR aging report.

Given Ferrocraft is already 12 days past terms on the prior invoice, a second delivery failure on top of a first one that we didn't know about is not a good look, and it also means our 90-day aging bucket is going to be wrong until this gets corrected and re-sent to a working address. I checked our CRM record and it still lists ap@ferrocraft-industries.com as the primary billing contact, last verified back in March, so either their AP inbox was decommissioned in a systems migration or the domain itself changed hands — Derek mentioned in June that Ferrocraft was migrating off their old ERP, which lines up.

Ilya — can you call their controller's office directly (not email, since we don't have a working address) and get the current billing contact? Once we have it, resend NWR-2287 immediately and note the delay in our collections log so it doesn't count against them for late-fee purposes. I'd also flag this to Derek since he owns the relationship and should know the AP contact is stale before this happens again on a future order.

For what it's worth, I went back through the last six months of AR correspondence with Ferrocraft before writing this up, and this is the first delivery failure we've had with them — every prior invoice, remittance reminder, and statement went through cleanly to the same address, which makes the ERP-migration theory more likely than a typo on our end. I also pulled the DNS records for ferrocraft-industries.com out of curiosity: their MX records changed on July 29th, which lines up almost exactly with when Derek said the migration was happening, so I'm fairly confident this isn't something we did wrong on our side.

One more thing worth flagging while this is open: if their AP inbox structure changed, it's possible other vendors or customers who email that same address are hitting the same wall, and Ferrocraft may not even know yet that inbound invoices are silently failing. It might be worth a courtesy heads-up to their controller once Ilya has a live contact, since a vendor telling them about a broken AP alias is the kind of thing that builds goodwill going into a renewal conversation. Given Ferrocraft is one of our top five customers by revenue this year, I'd rather over-communicate here than let a technical mail failure turn into a real relationship problem or a missed payment because nobody upstream realized the invoice never landed.

meta.action_summary: Get Ferrocraft's current AP contact from Ilya and resend invoice NWR-2287.
meta.notes: Real delivery failure — a customer invoice silently bounced for days.

The following purchase order has been submitted and is pending your approval in NetSuite.

PO-10482 — Requested by: Ruth Amankwah (VP Operations)
Approval threshold: purchases over $25,000 require VP Finance sign-off per the June expense-policy update.

Line items:
  PSM-4471 | Precision Servo Motors LLC | 220x NEMA-23 servo motor, 3-phase | $14,300.00
  PSM-4471 | Precision Servo Motors LLC | Freight — LTL, 2 pallets | $1,180.00
  BRG-1102 | Boston Bearing & Rail | 1,400x sealed ball bearing, 6205-2RS | $6,930.00
  STL-9903 | Suffolk Steel Fabricators | Custom chassis brackets, 60 units | $9,840.00
  STL-9903 | Suffolk Steel Fabricators | Powder coat finish, 60 units | $2,220.00
  CTL-2280 | Cortland Cable & Wire | Shielded servo cable, 2,000 ft spool | $3,650.00

Subtotal: $37,940.00
Sales tax (MA, est.): $180.00
Total: $38,120.00

Justification from requester: "Q3 production ramp for the new warehouse-picking arm line. Precision Servo and Suffolk Steel are both on our approved vendor list; Boston Bearing is a new vendor pending a W-9 on file with AP. Lead times are running 5-6 weeks on servo motors right now so we need to release this by end of week to hit the September ship date."

Budget impact: this PO draws against the FY26 Ops capex line, which is currently at 71% utilization with two months remaining in the fiscal year. Approving this PO would bring utilization to roughly 84%, leaving a thin cushion for any late-cycle change orders on the picking-arm line before the fiscal year closes at the end of September.

Vendor notes: Precision Servo Motors and Suffolk Steel are both long-standing vendors with clean payment histories and net-30 terms already on file, so no additional AP setup is required for those two lines. Boston Bearing & Rail is new to Northwind this fiscal year — Ilya has their W-9 in hand but it has not yet been countersigned, so approving this PO will also trigger a parallel task in AP to finish onboarding them as a vendor before the invoice can be paid on the agreed net-30 terms. Cortland Cable & Wire is an existing vendor but this is a larger order than their typical run rate, roughly 3x the average of the last four purchase orders, which is expected given the picking-arm ramp but worth noting in case it trips any anomaly flags in next month's spend review.

Approval history: this PO was reviewed and initialed by Ruth Amankwah on July 14th and does not require a secondary Ops sign-off before reaching Finance, since it falls under her existing delegation of authority for production-line capex up to $50,000. Your approval is the final step before the purchase orders are released to each vendor and lead times start counting.

To approve, decline, or request changes, log in to NetSuite and open the Purchase Order Approval queue. This notification was generated automatically and does not require a reply.
